sections.label: US Liberation Day tariffs
sections.summary: US 'Liberation Day' tariff announcements confirm the era of rules-based globalisation and free trade is over.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The recent "Liberation Day" tariff announcements by the United States (US) confirms this stark reality – the era of rules-based globalisation and free trade is over.

sections.label: US blanket and higher tariffs
sections.summary: The US imposed a blanket 10% tariff on nearly all countries, plus higher tariffs up to 50% on selected countries with trade surpluses.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The US has imposed a blanket 10% tariff on imports for nearly all countries.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On top of that, it has layered on higher tariffs, up to 50%, for selected countries, especially those that run a trade surplus with the US.

sections.label: Singapore tariff should be zero
sections.summary: If tariffs were truly reciprocal and targeted only trade surpluses, Singapore's tariff should be zero.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If the tariffs were truly reciprocal and if they were meant to target only those with trade surpluses, then the tariff for Singapore should be zero.

sections.label: Average US tariff on China
sections.summary: The average US tariff on Chinese products now exceeds 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Taken together, the average US tariff on Chinese products now exceeds 60%.

sections.label: Repudiation of MFN principle
sections.summary: America's new tariff regime is a complete repudiation of the MFN principle.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: America's new tariff regime is a complete repudiation of the MFN principle.

sections.label: Singapore no retaliatory tariffs
sections.summary: Singapore decided not to impose retaliatory tariffs, as doing so would only increase costs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Singapore has decided not to impose retaliatory tariffs.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Doing so will only lead to increased costs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Previous status quo restoration difficulty
sections.summary: It will be very hard to restore the previous status quo, and the 10% universal rate does not look open for negotiation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will be very hard to restore the previous status quo.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And in particular, it does not look like the 10% universal rate is open for negotiation.

sections.label: US and China tariff threats
sections.summary: The US has threatened an additional 50% tariff on China, and China says it will fight till the end.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The US has now threatened an additional 50% tariff on China and China says it will fight till the end.

sections.label: Weaker global growth expected
sections.summary: In the near term, weaker global growth is expected, meaning external demand for goods and services will fall.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the near term, we expect weaker global growth, which means external demand for our goods and services will fall.

sections.label: GDP growth forecast reassessment
sections.summary: Growth will be significantly impacted; MTI is reassessing the 2025 GDP growth forecast of 1% to 3% and will likely revise it downwards.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But I have no doubt that our growth will be significantly impacted.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We had originally projected GDP growth of 1% to 3% for 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) is reassessing the growth forecast and will likely revise it downwards.

sections.label: Task force for businesses and workers
sections.summary: A task force chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong will be set up to help businesses and workers address uncertainties and adapt.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the situation is fluid and can change quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, set up a task force chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong to help businesses and workers address the immediate uncertainties, strengthen their resilience and better adapt to the new economic environment.

sections.label: Special ASEAN Economic Ministers' Meeting
sections.summary: A Special ASEAN Economic Ministers' Meeting will be convened later this week.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A Special ASEAN Economic Ministers' Meeting will be convened later this week.

sections.label: Singapore's reserves, compact, resilience
sections.summary: Singapore is in a better position than 60 years ago, with deep reserves, a strong compact, and a never say die spirit.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In many ways, we are in a better position than we were 60 years ago when we became independent.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have built deep reserves as a strategic buffer.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have forged a strong compact, built on solidarity and trust in each other.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And most of all, we have our ingenuity and wit, our grit and gumption – a never say die spirit that has seen us through every crisis, and will carry us through the ones to come.

sections.label: Singapore as beacon of hope
sections.summary: In a dark and troubled world, Singapore will hold its ground as a beacon of stability, purpose and hope.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In a dark and troubled world, Singapore will hold our ground as a beacon of stability, purpose and hope.

sections.label: Budget, SkillsFuture, capability building
sections.summary: Budget resources go to strengthening the economy, innovation, new technologies, and SkillsFuture as a pillar of the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think similar announcements have been made by the Malaysian government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is an ongoing endeavour and in this year's Budget, we set aside more resources to doing so, especially to strengthen our economy, to build up our capabilities in innovation and new technologies, which are the key drivers for any economy to be strong, dynamic and vibrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At the same time, we are building capabilities in our people, investing in human capital, investing in our workers, upgrading the skills of our workers through SkillsFuture, and we are putting significant resources into this effort to make SkillsFuture a key part and a key pillar in our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the capability-building efforts will continue, in fact, we will redouble our efforts in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And the key reason why we are able to do all this is precisely because we have the fiscal resources to set aside.

sections.label: Medium-term economic and workforce restructure
sections.summary: In the medium to longer term, a major restructure of the economy will result in a restructure of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: It may not be immediately, but I think, in the medium to longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I think there will be a major restructure of the economy that will result in the restructure of the workforce as well.

sections.label: Tariff impact and trading partners
sections.summary: Assessing the total impact of tariffs takes time and must account for other countries' reactions, while Singapore reaches out to trading partners.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: It will take time for us to get to a better understanding, better assessment of the total impact of what is going to happen.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Also, we have to bear in mind that what would happen also has to take into account the reaction from the countries other than America, so their reaction will also add on to the potential impact on the tariffs and on Singapore's economy, and at the same time, we are also reaching out to our trading partners to share our information, share our assessment of the situation, to see how we can find different ways of working together, to continue to do business with one another, to continue to provide opportunities for businesses and for our enterprises.

sections.label: US 10% tariff view
sections.summary: It is their view that every country should have at least a 10% tariff, and Singapore continues conversations with the US and other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is their view of the world and they have decided that every country should at least have a 10% tariff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we are continuing to have these conversations with the US administration and also with other countries.

sections.label: Finding new export markets
sections.summary: Singapore will help companies find new export markets in the Middle East and Latin America, but expects slower growth if trade barriers rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On where else will there be new markets for our exports, well, we will continue to find export markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will help our companies identify new markets, including areas that they may not be so familiar with, and that is why we are redoubling our efforts to strengthen our links, including in areas in the Middle East, in Latin America, areas where we may not have such close links, but we think there is potential and opportunities to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But fundamentally, we have to be prepared that if trade barriers around the world are higher than they were before, then, ultimately, we are entering a world where there will be slower growth, less demand for our goods and services.

sections.label: Budget measures and trade negotiation
sections.summary: Budget measures are deemed adequate for now, with Deputy Prime Minister Gan's task force monitoring and recommending later, while trade negotiation via ASEAN or CPTPP is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For now, we think that the Budget measures are adequate, but the task force chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan will monitor, will assess and will put up recommendations when ready.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For trade, I wonder if the Government will be looking to negotiate within the broader rubric of ASEAN or the CPTPP as a block?

sections.label: ASEAN and CPTPP trade strategy
sections.summary: Singapore is working with ASEAN members, CPTPP partners and other trade organisations to discuss strategy towards the US, with an ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting on 10 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, on external trade relationships, indeed, we are working with ASEAN members as well as our fellow CPTPP partners, as well as other trade organisations, to see how we can come together to discuss our strategy towards the US, how we can negotiate and discuss as an organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We announced that we are going to have the ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting shortly, if I am not wrong, on 10 April.

sections.label: Anti-dumping duties and consumer cost
sections.summary: Anti-dumping duties are a WTO possibility, but imposing them means Singapore consumers pay the duty, adding cost to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In terms of anti-dumping duties, it is a possibility provided under the WTO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But you also have to bear in mind that by imposing anti-dumping duties, that means consumers in Singapore will be paying the duty for the imports and that will add cost to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Task force engaging businesses
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan's task force will engage businesses to understand the unfolding impact and work out additional measures needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we think the concerns have to be dealt with quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And so, Deputy Prime Minister Gan's task force will continue to engage businesses to better understand the full extent of the impact, because this situation is still unfolding; and eventually, to work out what additional measures we need.

sections.label: Semiconductor exports to US share
sections.summary: Singapore's semiconductor exports to the US were about 8.9% of total goods exports to the US and 0.8% of total goods exports worldwide in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our semi-conductor exports to the US comprises about 8.9% of Singapore's total goods exports to the US and this is equivalent to 0.8% of Singapore's total goods exports to the world in 2024.

sections.label: ASEAN non-tariff barrier reduction
sections.summary: ASEAN Economic Ministers will discuss the region's position, while efforts to reduce non-tariff barriers within ASEAN should be redoubled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As for what position ASEAN takes as a whole, the ASEAN Economic Ministers are meeting soon and they will discuss further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But one key step that we can take, quite aside from engaging America as a collective, is really to redouble our efforts, work even harder to reduce non-tariff barriers within ASEAN itself.

sections.label: Tariffs hard to reverse
sections.summary: Raised tariffs are historically hard to bring back down, and the administration has said the base tier is not for negotiation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And when tariffs are raised, it is usually, as you look at the historical record, very hard for them to come back down again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And in any case, the administration has already indicated the base tier is not for negotiation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are engaging them, but if that is truly their position, then these are not temporary tariffs at all.

sections.label: Investment on commercial merits
sections.summary: Projects are evaluated strictly on their own merits, not diplomatic or political considerations, and Singapore will not compromise its commercial investment principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whether the imports in the months to come come from China or from other countries where the duties are substantially higher, how will the Government be able to support domestic companies without any form of anti-dumping duties, keeping in mind that the margins are razor thin already, especially for our SMEs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They evaluate projects strictly on their own merits, not for diplomatic or political considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, they will continue with that approach and if indeed, the continued investments that we are making, that Singapore as a whole is making in the US, help to advance a bilateral relationship, so much the better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we will not compromise our key principles of investing on a proper basis, commercial basis and evaluating projects on the basis that they are fundamentally good investment projects for Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore attracts investment pipeline
sections.summary: In previous crises and slowdowns, Singapore continued to attract a healthy pipeline of investments because of its reputation as a trusted business hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At least in previous crises and slowdowns, we have continued to be able to attract a good and healthy pipeline of investments because Singapore's reputation as a trusted business hub is strong and companies do want to do more activities out of Singapore.

sections.label: Companies holding back new projects
sections.summary: Many companies are holding back on new projects, not because they do not want to come to Singapore, but because of uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: What we do hear, for now, is that many are holding back – not so much that they do not want to come to Singapore, but they are just holding back on new projects, precisely because of the uncertainty that I highlighted just now.

sections.label: World need not follow US
sections.summary: Even if the US abandons the WTO and takes a more protectionist path, the rest of the world does not have to follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my Statement, even if the US has chosen to abandon the WTO, to reject WTO rules and to go in a more protectionist path, the rest of the world does not have to follow.

sections.label: Supply chain reorganisation and investments
sections.summary: The task force strategy covers shorter and longer term supply chain reorganisation, requiring increased logistics and capacity, more investments anchored in Singapore, and a shifting trade balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Certainly, I think this is part and parcel of the task force's strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are looking at both the shorter term as well as the longer term, and some of these supply chain reorganisation will take some time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Logistics and some capacity have to be increased in order to open up new markets and new sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, I think some of these will take time to reorganise and that will happen in the medium to longer term, working with the industries, trying to attract more investments so that they are anchored in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But always also bear in mind, as we have more investments into Singapore and taking advantage of a lower tariff, as the Member mentioned, to export to the US, our trade balance would start to shift.

sections.label: Engaging countries to keep WTO system
sections.summary: Singapore engages like-minded countries in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, needing other big players to keep the WTO system and rules-based trading going.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: While Singapore can try to do our best to speak up, to carrel and to engage like-minded countries, let us be realistic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are not going to be able to fill the vacuum ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We need other big players to step in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we are engaging all of them in Europe, in Asia, in the Middle East and hopefully, together as a coalition or as a broader, wider group of countries, there will be enough voices that share a common interest in keeping the WTO system going, updating it and maintaining our rules-based trading system.

sections.label: FTA zero tariff and US emergency powers
sections.summary: The FTA provides zero tariffs both sides, so import duty violates it, though economic emergency allows tariffs, and the US has invoked emergency economic powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The FTA provides for zero tariff on both sides – the US for us and us for imports from the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, any imposition of import duty is a violation of the FTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the event of an economic emergency, you have the right to invoke that provision to allow you to put in place measures, including tariffs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And our understanding is that the US has now invoked emergency economic powers.

sections.label: Possible counter-import duties under FTA
sections.summary: Singapore may consider action under the FTA allowing counter-import duties on US imports, but does not anticipate import duties on US imports for now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And eventually, whether or not we want to take action is something that we will have to consider and if we need to take actions under the FTA that allows us to introduce counter-import duties on imports from the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have already said that we do not anticipate the introduction of import duties on imports from the US for the time being.

sections.label: ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting on US
sections.summary: Singapore is talking to ASEAN counterparts and will hold an ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting on 10 April to discuss engaging the US collectively as ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I think this is something that I mentioned earlier that we are working on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are talking to our ASEAN counterparts and we are going to have our ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting on 10 April to discuss this, how do we approach this issue, how can we engage the US collectively as ASEAN.
